subject.title: fix: block no-auth managed gateway LAN installs

question: Should OpenClaw accept an install-time fail-closed block for explicit gateway.auth.mode none when the managed Gateway bind resolves outside loopback?
rationale: The code matches the existing runtime security boundary, but it changes a setup/refresh path so existing invalid managed installs fail earlier and require operator action before service rewrite.

options.title: Accept earlier install block
options.body: Land the PR as the narrower managed-install guard because it matches the current runtime refusal and gives operators an actionable remediation before the service is rewritten.

options.title: Require fuller service proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted Windows Scheduled Task or equivalent managed-service refresh run on the branch before accepting the compatibility change.

options.title: Pause for broader update proof
options.body: Keep the PR paused if maintainers want the unproven update-mutation claim solved before changing the install boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept earlier install block
recommendation.body: Land the PR as the narrower managed-install guard because it matches the current runtime refusal and gives operators an actionable remediation before the service is rewritten.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest live history across the exposed Gateway startup guard and daemon install/auth boundary touched by the PR.
